_README: Per-model API prices in USD per 1,000,000 tokens. EDIT THIS FILE to fix/add prices — keys are the model id (lowercased; any leading 'moonshotai/' is stripped automatically). Each entry: input = normal (uncached) input, cachedInput = cache-hit input (cheaper), cacheWrite = one-time cache-creation surcharge (Anthropic only; 0 for providers that don't charge it), output = generated tokens. For peak/off-peak billing (DeepSeek V4), the base fields are OFF-PEAK rates and the optional peakInput/peakCachedInput/peakOutput/peakHoursUtc fields carry the peak rates plus the [startHour,endHour) UTC windows. A model NOT listed here shows a muted '$' whose tooltip tells you to add it. Local models are ignored entirely. CONFIDENCE: gpt-5.6-*, claude-fable-5, claude-fable-5-1, claude-mythos-5, claude-mythos-5-1, and dola-seed-2-1-turbo are from published prices; Claude opus/sonnet/haiku use the standard Anthropic structure (cached=0.1x input, cacheWrite=1.25x input) with generation-4 numbers; EVERYTHING ELSE (Kimi, Gemini, Grok, GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen, MiniMax, Cohere, MiMo, older GPT-5) is a ROUGH ESTIMATE — verify against each provider's pricing page and correct here. NOTE (2026-09-02, verified against platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing): Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 use a special 0.025x cache-hit multiplier (cachedInput=0.25) instead of the standard 0.1x — this is their headline pricing change over Fable 5/Mythos 5, whose cachedInput stays at the standard 1.0. cacheWrite=12.5 for all four fable/mythos entries is the official 5-minute cache-write rate (1.25x input); Anthropic also offers a 1-hour cache write at 2x input ($20) which this single-field schema cannot represent — 5-minute was chosen as the more common default. The previous claude-fable-5/mythos-5 cacheWrite value of 18.75 did not match either official rate and has been corrected to 12.5. NOTE (2026-09-23, verified against the Anthropic pricing docs): claude-opus-5-5 is $4 input / $20 output with a cache HIT at $0.20 — that is 0.05x input, NOT the standard 0.1x, so it is the same kind of special cache-hit multiplier Fable 5.1 introduced. Its cacheWrite=5 is the 5-minute rate (1.25x input); the 1-hour rate would be 8. NEXUS sends cache_control without a ttl field, which means the 5-minute TTL, so the 5-minute write rate is the correct one for every Anthropic row here. CORRECTIONS (2026-09-23, same docs page): three Anthropic cacheWrite/input values were wrong and are fixed. (a) claude-sonnet-5 cacheWrite was 4 — that is the 1-HOUR rate; the 5-minute rate is 2.50. (b) claude-haiku-4-5 (undated) was {input 3, cachedInput 0.3, cacheWrite 2.2} — nothing in that row matched any published Haiku 4.5 price, and the row IS reachable (it is the default eyes model and the default subagent model), so eyes/subagent cost was over-reported ~3x. Correct: $1 / $0.10 / $1.25 / $5. (c) claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 cacheWrite was 2, again the 1-hour rate; corrected to 1.25. Verified-correct and left alone: opus-5/4-8/4-7, sonnet-4-6, fable/mythos 5 and 5.1. NOTE (2026-10-02, verified against the same pricing docs page): claude-sonnet-5-5 was added and is priced IDENTICALLY to claude-sonnet-5 — $2 input / $0.20 cache-hit / $2.50 5-minute cacheWrite / $10 output. Its $0.20 cache hit is the STANDARD 0.1x (0.1 x $2), NOT a special multiplier — footnote 2 on the docs page gives the 0.05x special only to Opus 5.5; Sonnet 5.5 uses the standard multiplier. Same visit re-confirmed opus-5-5 ($4/$0.20/$5/$20) and sonnet-5 ($2/$0.20/$2.50/$10) against the live table.
_NOTE_kimi: Verified 2026-09-19 against platform.kimi.ai/docs (pricing page) and a live GET /v1/models on api.moonshot.ai. The token API catalog is exactly four ids: kimi-k3, kimi-k2.7-code, kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed, kimi-k2.6. kimi-k2.5 is RETIRED (404 on retrieve and on call) — its row is kept only so old conversations still cost out, and its numbers were never re-verified against an official page. There is no kimi-k2.8 on the token API in any spelling; 'K2.8 Preview' ships only inside the Kimi Code / Kimi Work subscription (api.kimi.com/coding/v1, served under the id kimi-for-coding), which is flat-rate and therefore has no per-token row here.
_NOTE_gemini-4-argon: Reachable from 2026-10-14 (announced 2026-09-30; on 2026-10-08 every id spelling still 404'd across v1/v1beta/v1alpha). Prices read off ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing on 2026-10-14, quoted verbatim: input '$2.00 through November 30, 2026. $4.00 starting December 1, 2026.', output '$10.00 through November 30, 2026. $20.00 starting December 1, 2026.', context caching '$0.10 through November 30, 2026. $0.20 starting December 1, 2026.'. Numbers below are the CURRENT introductory rate — REVISIT ON 2026-12-01, when all three double. cachedInput here is the published $0.10 (5% of input), NOT the 25%-of-input convention used for the 3.x siblings: that convention exists because Google never published their cached rate, whereas argon's is on the price page. Catalogue (GetModel, 2026-10-14): in=1048576, out=32768 — half the 65536 output ceiling of every 3.x sibling. NEXUS never sends maxOutputTokens on the Gemini path, so the provider default applies and the Gemini branch's 5 automatic continuations absorb it.
_NOTE_gemini-3.8-flash: Released 2026-09-02 (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/latest-model). Introductory pricing $0.75/$3.75 (input/output per 1M) in effect through 2026-12-31; reverts to standard $1.50/$7.50 (same as 3.6 Flash) after that. Numbers below use the CURRENT introductory rate — revisit after the cutover date. cachedInput follows the same 25%-of-input convention used for its Gemini siblings (some third-party writeups say '90% discount', but that doesn't match the pattern Nexus already uses across 3.5/3.6/3.7 Flash, so the codebase convention was kept for consistency).
_NOTE_gemini-3.7-flash: Introductory pricing $0.75/$3.75 (input/output per 1M) in effect through 2026-12-31; reverts to standard $1.50/$7.50 (same as 3.6 Flash) after that. Numbers below use the CURRENT introductory rate — revisit after the cutover date.
_NOTE_grok: xAI bills the whole Grok line on a CLIFF-EDGE threshold, not a blended/tiered rate: prompts under 200K tokens pay the rates below; the moment ANY part of a request crosses 200K tokens, the ENTIRE request rebills at DOUBLE those rates. This flat schema has no field for that — numbers below are the UNDER-200K rate, so any turn that crosses the threshold shows as under-priced here. Flagged for Lizard-kun rather than guessed at. Context windows: grok-4.7 / 4.6 / 4.5 = 500K; grok-4.3 and the 4.20 family = 1M. Rates verified 2026-09-23 against the xAI /v1/language-models catalog (its price fields are in units of 1e-4 USD per 1M tokens) and the published docs; the 4.5 and 4.3 rows had been overstated and were corrected in the same pass.
_NOTE_glm-5.3-flash: GLM-5.3-Flash: first natively multimodal GLM-5 model (image + video + file input, 1M context). Numbers below are the LIST prices. Z.AI is running a 50% intro discount through 2026-09-09 24:00 UTC+8 (input $0.075 / cached $0.015 / output $0.25) — after the cutover it reverts to these list prices ($0.15 / $0.03 / $0.50). Revisit after 2026-09-09.
_NOTE_deepseek-v4: DeepSeek uses PEAK/OFF-PEAK pricing (since 2026-08-16 16:00 UTC). Off-peak = half of peak. Peak hours: 01:00-04:00 + 06:00-10:00 UTC, Monday-Friday (weekends are off-peak). Base fields below (input/cachedInput/output) are OFF-PEAK; the peak* fields hold peak rates and peakHoursUtc holds the [startHour,endHour) UTC ranges. input = cache-MISS, cachedInput = cache-HIT, cacheWrite = 0 (DeepSeek charges no cache-write surcharge).
_NOTE_deepseek-flash: FLASH-SERIES REPRICE effective 2026-09-10 12:00 Beijing (04:00 UTC): off-peak cache-hit $0.003 / cache-miss $0.15 / output $0.6 per 1M; peak = double. That is a ~57% cut from the old Flash rates (0.007 / 0.22 / 0.66) which these rows carried until 2026-09-14. VERIFIED LIVE against api.deepseek.com on 2026-09-14, not recalled. GET /models now returns exactly TWO ids: 'deepseek-flash' (= DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 1M context, max_tokens range [1,393216], vision YES, thinking enabled/disabled both accepted) and 'deepseek-v4-pro' (= V4-Pro-0813, pricing UNCHANGED, vision NO). 'deepseek-v4-flash', 'deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp', 'deepseek-chat' and 'deepseek-reasoner' are still ACCEPTED and are served by V4.1-Flash at the Flash price, so they carry the same rates here. 'deepseek-v4-flash-0731' is now a hard 400 upstream; NEXUS remaps it to 'deepseek-flash' on the wire, so its row is kept and repriced to match what is actually billed today (historical 0731 traffic from before 2026-09-10 was billed at DOUBLE these rates - the table has no date dimension, so old conversations using that id now under-report). Images are billed as input tokens by dimension: measured 64x64 -> 197 prompt tokens, 512x512 -> 197, 1024x768 -> 509; treat 1024 tokens/image as the upper bound (the old ~384 figure was for the retired vision-exp model).
_NOTE_qwen3.8-max: PUBLISHED prices (not an estimate). Model Studio lists input $2, output $6, implicit-cache hit $0.25, explicit-cache creation $2.50, explicit-cache hit $0.17. NEXUS never creates an explicit DashScope cache, so cachedInput uses the IMPLICIT hit price ($0.25) and cacheWrite is 0. If explicit caching is ever wired for DashScope, change these to 0.17 / 2.5.
_NOTE_mimo: Verified 2026-09-22 against mimo.mi.com/docs/en-US/pricing (Overseas Pay-As-You-Go, Update Time September 21 2026). The V2.6 series is priced identically to the V2.5 series — mimo-v2.6-pro shares its row with mimo-v2.5-pro, and mimo-v2.6-flash shares its row with mimo-v2.5. mimo-v2.5-pro and mimo-v2.5 are officially deprecated at 10:00 Beijing time on 2026-10-21; their rows are kept so past conversations still cost correctly. The previous V2.5 numbers here (0.3/1.2 for both tiers) were rough estimates and were wrong in both directions: v2.5-pro input was under-reported and output over-reported, and v2.5 was charged at the pro tier's rate. Batch API halves the rates (not modelled — NEXUS does not use it). Cache write is free. Web search plugin is billed separately at $5/1000 calls.
_NOTE_muse-spark: Meta Model API (api.meta.ai/v1). Standard tier $1.25 input / $4.25 output / $0.15 cached input per 1M; Contributor tier $0.10 / $0.20 / $0.002. Cache WRITE is free — measured 2026-10-05: cache_creation_input_tokens was 0 on the call that created the cache, and the next call read it (cache_read 3569 of a 3614-token prefix), so there is no separate write charge to model. CONTRIBUTOR IS A DIFFERENT MODEL ID, not an account setting: picking a `-contributor` row opts Meta into training on that turn's prompts AND completions, and drops the rate limit to ~60 rpm / ~250k tokens per day (standard is 3,000 rpm / 4M tokens per minute — the latter read verbatim off x-ratelimit-limit-* response headers). PRICE SOURCE, honestly: the standard/contributor numbers are documented for 1.1 and 1.2 only; Meta's own pricing page sits behind an SSO login and the API exposes no billing/credits endpoint (/v1/credits, /v1/usage, /v1/billing and four other conventional paths all 404), so 1.3 is ASSUMED to match 1.1/1.2 and is NOT confirmed by a primary source. Revisit if a public price page appears.
